title: POSS-based hybrid biomaterials for tissue engineering and regenerative medicine

sections.heading: The preparation method, structure and properties of POSSHB used in regenerative medicine
sections.text: 2 The preparation method, structure and properties of POSSHB used in regenerative medicine 2.1 The preparation method and structure of POSSHB used in regenerative medicine In the field of regenerative medicine, the latest preparation methods for POSSHB mainly include the following:  covalent grafting modification:  POSS is covalently attached to polymers or biomolecules through chemical reactions, such as using the epoxy groups on the surface of POSS to react with amino groups (-NH 2 ) or hydroxyl groups (-OH), and graft onto degradable polymers such as polylactic acid (PLA) or polycaprolactone (PCL) to enhance mechanical properties [ 20 ].  Click Chemistry:  CuAAC (copper catalyzed azide alkyne cycloaddition) or thiol-ene reaction is used to achieve efficient and highly selective POSS functionalization for the preparation of biosensors or drug carriers [ 21 , 22 ].  Block copolymer synthesis:  POSS is used as a monomer to participate in polymerization, such as POSS polyurethane (PU): POSS reacts with isocyanates to form hard segment reinforced elastomers for artificial blood vessels or heart valves [ 23 , 24 ]. Alternatively, POSS-PEG amphiphilic block copolymers can be constructed to prepare hydrogels for tissue repair [ 25 , 26 ].  Physical blending method:  POSS is directly dispersed into polymer matrices (such as PLA, PCL, polyvinyl alcohol), and material properties are improved by solution casting or melt blending, such as enhancing mechanical strength or regulating degradation rate [ 27 ]. To adapt to different biological application scenarios, POSSHB can be prepared into different structures, such as hydrogels, 3D printing scaffolds, bone cements, electrospun fibers, films, nanoparticles,  etc . ( Fig. 1 ).  POSSHB hydrogel:  POSSHB hydrogel is prepared by covalent bonding or physical blending, which shows superior performance characteristics to traditional hydrogel. In terms of structural design, the introduction of POSS can form a denser three-dimensional network structure. For example, the pore diameter of pH responsive SA/PEGDA/AS-POSS hydrogel prepared by Michael addition reaction decreases with the increase of POSS content, and the compression modulus increases significantly. This structural characteristic enables its drug loading to reach 85.7 % and achieves a cumulative release rate of 80.4 % in weakly acidic environments, demonstrating excellent potential for tumor targeted therapy [ 28 , 29 ]. In terms of functional characteristics, POSSHB hydrogel has three advantages: first, intelligent responsiveness, such as pH, temperature or enzyme triggered release; Secondly, the mechanical properties have been significantly enhanced; The third is good biocompatibility, with a cell survival rate generally exceeding 90 %. In particular, POSS-SH based hydrogel microspheres are prepared by microfluidic technology, which can effectively improve the bioavailability of insoluble drugs and promote the differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells into chondrocytes. However, these materials still face the challenge of uncontrollable degradation behavior, especially hydrolysis in alkaline environments. POSSHB-3D printing scaffold : In the field of 3D printing, POSSHB can be directly incorporated into printing materials as a modifier to construct special structures. Research has shown that 3-thiopropyl polysilsesquioxane (SSQ-SH) can increase the elongation at break of PLA by 56 % and impact strength by 37 % within the concentration range of 1-1.5 wt%, while maintaining good printability [ 30 ]. More innovative is the design of the "stiffness memory" scaffold. Through 3D printing guided thermally induced phase separation (3DTIPS) technology, POSS polyurethane scaffolds exhibit unique dynamic mechanical properties: providing sufficient mechanical support during implantation and gradually softening to match tissue modulus. This characteristic can significantly reduce stress shielding effects and promote organizational integration. However, the dispersion uniformity of POSS remains a key challenge, as concentrations exceeding 2.5 wt% can easily lead to agglomeration [ 31 ]. POSSHB bone cement : Traditional bone cement (such as PMMA) has problems such as high heat generation and toxic residue, while POSSHB bone cement completely avoids these defects through click on chemistry (click ON) and catalyst free SPAAC reaction cross-linking [ 32 , 33 ]. This type of material has three major breakthrough advantages: firstly, its biological safety is significantly improved, and it only produces mild inflammatory reactions after implantation; Secondly, porous structures (porosity>60 %) can be constructed through salt leaching and other methods to promote cell infiltration and vascular growth; Most importantly, it can load growth factors (such as BMP-2/VEGF) and nano hydroxyapatite, demonstrating osteogenic effects comparable to autogenous bone in a rabbit spinal fusion model [ 34 ]. But the main obstacle faced by clinical translation is insufficient mechanical strength. POSSHB electrospun fibers : In the field of electrospinning, the introduction of POSS nanoparticles can significantly enhance the hydrophobicity and thermal stability of electrospun fibers, improve their oil absorption performance and recyclability. For example, POSS coated polylactic acid electrospun nanofiber membranes exhibit excellent performance in oil-water separation [ 35 ]. In addition, POSS-PCUU electrospun fiber modified with ESPA protein can significantly promote endothelial cell adhesion and the expression of related markers (VE cadherin, VEGFR-2), making them suitable for small caliber vascular transplantation [ 36 ]. Long term stability remains the main obstacle to clinical application, and in the future, cross-linking strategies need to be developed to enhance the durability of fibers in bodily fluid environments. POSSHB film : POSS conjugated polymer hybrid films not only exhibit thermally stable white light emission properties, but also have good biocompatibility, making them suitable for fields such as optoelectronic devices and biosensors [ 37 ]. In addition, POSS modified Ti 3 C 2 T x  MXene films and chitosan-silver-octa ammonium-POSS composite films also exhibit excellent antibacterial properties and biocompatibility, making them suitable for surface modification of biomedical materials [ 38 , 39 ]. The optimization of mechanical properties of thin film materials is still a research focus, especially the balance between flexibility and strength. POSSHB nanoparticles : The application of POSS based nanoparticles in the biomedical field mainly focuses on drug delivery and photothermal therapy. For example, POSS-SQ NPs exhibit a high photothermal conversion efficiency of 67.2 %, far exceeding most organic photothermal agents [ 40 ]. More noteworthy is the PSD-FA intelligent nanoplatform, which integrates the triple functions of folate targeting, GSH responsive release, and photothermal therapy, achieving a tumor inhibition rate of 74.7 % in animal experiments [ 41 ]. The challenge of this type of material lies in the unclear metabolic behavior  in vivo , and future systematic pharmacokinetic studies are needed. Optimizing PEG modification strategies (such as degradable PEG) may improve its biological distribution. In summary, significant progress has been made in the application of POSSHB in the field of biomedical regeneration. Whether in the preparation of hydrogels, 3D printing scaffolds, bone cements, electrospun fibers, films or nanoparticles, POSSHB has shown its unique advantages and huge application potential. 2.2 Mechanical properties Mechanical properties are key parameters for designing tissue engineering scaffolds for bone tissue regeneration [ [42] ,  [43] ,  [44] ,  [45] ]. For example, as a bone substitute, the mechanical properties of the implants should match those of the tissue defect to protect the cells from destructive compression or stretching, allowing cells to develop into normal tissue. At the same time, the “stress shielding” effect should be avoided [ 46 ]. And when it is used as a nerve scaffold, the suitable flexibility can adapt to the movement of the human body, so as to avoid the physical damage caused by improper position [ 47 ]. Additionally, it should be able to bear the repeated compressive force of surrounding tissue without obvious deformation. Studies have shown that the stiffness of scaffolds can influence cell behavior [ 48 ]. The rigid nano core and multi reactive groups carried by POSS can provide a broad platform for the preparation of composite materials with adjustable and controllable mechanical properties. POSS is generally used as a filler to modify the mechanical properties of other matrix materials (synthetic polymers, natural polymers, inorganic biomaterials, and so on), especially for the synthetic polymers (polycarbonate (PC), PLA, polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), melt spun polyester based composite fiber, PNIPAM, PCL, and so on) [ [49] ,  [50] ,  [51] ,  [52] ,  [53] ]. The content of POSS has an important effect on the mechanical properties of the composites. For example, triphenyl-POSS and amino propyl isobutyl-POSS were respectively introduced into PC and PLA by melt blending method. In a low range, the tensile properties and dynamic mechanical modulus of the composites were improved with the increase of POSS content [ 54 , 55 ]. Amna et al. found that POSS nanoparticles exhibit effective nucleation effects, significantly improving the mechanical and thermal stability as well as biocompatibility of composite materials [ 56 ]. The same trend was also observed in other POSS-based hybrid materials, indicating that POSS acted as plasticizer and intensifier respectively with different content of POSS in the matrix materials [ 57 , 58 ]. In short, changing the POSS content can regulate the bending strength [ 59 ], tensile strength [ 60 , 61 ], elongation at break [ 61 , 62 ], and storage modulus [ 63 ] of the substrate material. In addition to the factors of the preparation method and the content of POSS, POSS with different end groups also affect the mechanical properties. Zhao et al. modified sodium-montmorillonite (MMT) with aminopropylisooctyl-POSS (AP-POSS) and octa ammonium-POSS (OA-POSS) respectively that could effectively control the dispersion of MTT and improve the mechanical properties of the composites by 60 % and 10 %, respectively [ 64 ]. Humeyra Sirin et al. compared the effects of POSS type and content on the mechanical properties of melt-spun polyester-based composite fibers (PET). When the content of hydroxyl-POSS was 1 wt%, the tensile modulus of the composite was increased fivefold due to the higher level of crystalline content and more oriented amorphous domains within the material. In addition, epoxy-POSS doubled the tensile modulus of PET composite fiber, while amine-POSS had no significant effect on the mechanical properties of PET [ 65 ]. The chemical structure of POSS affected its dispersion level, and then affected the mechanical properties of the composites. Octa-isobutyl-POSS was non-reactive and non-polar, and had the best dispersion among other reactive and polar POSS [ 66 ]. Additionally, Octa (3-chloroamonium propyl) silsesquioxane (OCAPS) as a physical crosslinker can enhance the toughness and compression properties of hydrogels [ 67 ]. Moreover, by incorporating bis-functionalized glycidyl propyl POSS (G-POSS) into the epoxy polymer backbone, the polymer chains are induced to self-assemble into a three-dimensional (3D) connected porous structure, significantly enhancing the mechanical properties of the material [ 68 ]. In conclusion, the mechanical strength of POSSHB can be adjusted according to the requirement of application due to the rigid character of the inorganic structure of POSS and the multi-reaction of the organic structure, which provides a strong support for the design of ideal biomedical materials. 2.3 Biodegradation behavior Biodegradation behavior of biomaterials is subjected to a series of reactions, such as hydrolysis, enzymatic hydrolysis and oxidation with the biological environment of body fluids, organic macromolecules, enzymes, free radicals, cells and so on, and gradually degraded to low molecular compounds or monomers. And then the degradation products are discharged out of the body or participate in the body's normal metabolism [ 69 ]. In comparison with natural polymers, chemical synthetic degradable materials can be used in practical applications by selecting suitable monomers or controlling the reaction conditions in the synthesis process to achieve the goal of synthesis materials [ 70 ]. POSS has significant advantages in designing ideal biodegradable biomaterials due to its unique nano-size effect and multi-reactive sites. Previous studies showed that PCL degradation was inhibited  in vitro  by POSS/PEO hybrid materials. POSS has been incorporated into many biodegradable materials and thermosetting biodegradable elastomers [ [71] ,  [72] ,  [73] ,  [74] ]. The biodegradable POSS-PCL star polymers were prepared by ring-opening polymerization of ε-caprolactone and octahydroxysiloxane, respectively by Sunny et al. The ratio of POSS and polymer can be customized to obtain polymers with ideal properties to meet tissue applications under different case conditions [ 75 ]. Erin et al. designed a linear polyurethane elastomer with short, biodegradable soft-segment and hard-segment POSS [ 76 ]. The soft segments can be introduced to control the degradation (such as PCL), while POSS will act as a physical cross-linker to link the adjacent chains together. In this way, elastomer properties can be designed by controlling the proportion of soft segments and POSS. Bagheri developed a POSS-polycaprolactone-zeolite (POSS-PCL-zeolite) nanocomposite using electrospinning technology. This POSS-PCL-zeolite nano scaffold has good biodegradability, can support the attachment and proliferation of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs), and induce bone differentiation [ 77 ]. In addition, Yong and his team electrospun a solution containing octaglycidyl polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxanes (Ope-POSS), 2-ethyl-4-methylimidazole (EMI), and PNIPAM. The resulting PNIPAM nanofiber network simulates the morphology of natural extracellular matrix (ECM), characterized by appropriate fiber diameter, pore size, and high overall porosity. It is worth noting that these nanofibers exhibit stability in aqueous environments, experiencing gradual mass loss rather than immediate dissolution, demonstrating significantly good water stability [ 78 ]. In a word, the degradation performance of POSSHB can be regulated and processed, which can meet the function demand of biomedicine and make it widely used in many fields of biomedicine. 2.4 Bioactivity in tissue regeneration POSSHB not only meet the basic requirements of tissue engineering in terms of structural design, mechanical properties, and biodegradability, but also the biological properties of the materials themselves have gradually become one of the key properties of concern in the field of tissue engineering. These characteristics include promoting cell adhesion and proliferation, inducing osteogenic differentiation, accelerating angiogenesis, enhancing growth factor release capacity, and exhibiting antibacterial and anti-inflammatory effects( Fig. 2 ). Fig. 2 The biological properties and regenerative medicine applications of POSSHB. Fig. 2 An injectable and biodegradable poly (propylene fumarate)- co -POSS hybrid copolymer was synthesized by covalently linking POSS to the main chain of poly (propylene fumarate). When the concentration of POSS was 10 %, MC3T3-E1 showed more remarkable ability of cell attachment, proliferation and differentiation [ 79 ]. In addition, Engstrand et al. copolymerized POSS with polyethylene glycol (PEG) to form injectable bone cement (POSS-PEG), which has similar strength to commercial cement. After soaking in PBS for 28 days, calcium deficient hydroxyapatite grew on the surface of the hybrid material [ 80 ]. A porous silicified polyvinyl acetate-POSS composite nanofibers were prepared by a simple electrospinning technique by Ha et al., which could support cell adhesion and guide the proliferation of myoblasts. The composite POSS-based nanofibers could be used as a potential matrix for osteoblast proliferation and mineralization to promote bone regeneration [ 81 ]. Based on the excellent biocompatibility and controllable mechanical properties of POSS, other multifunctional components were introduced into POSS, such as antibacterial Ag ion [ 82 ], anti-UV poly (p-phenylene terephthalamide) [ 83 ] or plasmids, so as to achieve tissue repair and regeneration. Liu et al. added POSS and isobutyl terminated peptides, as well as POSS poly (lysine-co-valine) (PKV) and isobutyl poly (lysine-co-valine) (KV), to a polycaprolactone solution for electrospinning, endowing the electrospun membrane with antibacterial properties for biomedical applications and potential applications in vascular transplantation or wound healing [ 84 ]. The biological activity of POSSHB is a key factor in its application in tissue engineering. By promoting cell adhesion, proliferation, and differentiation, inducing angiogenesis, as well as antibacterial and anti-inflammatory functions, POSSHB can effectively simulate the microenvironment of natural tissues and accelerate tissue repair. This characteristic of combining structural support and biological activity has demonstrated significant advantages for POSSHB in fields such as bone repair, soft tissue regeneration, and infection control, providing an important direction for the development of the next generation of intelligent biomaterials.

Click Chemistry:  CuAAC (copper catalyzed azide alkyne cycloaddition) or thiol-ene reaction is used to achieve efficient and highly selective POSS functionalization for the preparation of biosensors or drug carriers [ 21 , 22 ].  Block copolymer synthesis:  POSS is used as a monomer to participate in polymerization, such as POSS polyurethane (PU): POSS reacts with isocyanates to form hard segment reinforced elastomers for artificial blood vessels or heart valves [ 23 , 24 ]. Alternatively, POSS-PEG amphiphilic block copolymers can be constructed to prepare hydrogels for tissue repair [ 25 , 26 ].  Physical blending method:  POSS is directly dispersed into polymer matrices (such as PLA, PCL, polyvinyl alcohol), and material properties are improved by solution casting or melt blending, such as enhancing mechanical strength or regulating degradation rate [ 27 ]. To adapt to different biological application scenarios, POSSHB can be prepared into different structures, such as hydrogels, 3D printing scaffolds, bone cements, electrospun fibers, films, nanoparticles,  etc . ( Fig. 1 ).  POSSHB hydrogel:  POSSHB hydrogel is prepared by covalent bonding or physical blending, which shows superior performance characteristics to traditional hydrogel. In terms of structural design, the introduction of POSS can form a denser three-dimensional network structure. For example, the pore diameter of pH responsive SA/PEGDA/AS-POSS hydrogel prepared by Michael addition reaction decreases with the increase of POSS content, and the compression modulus increases significantly. This structural characteristic enables its drug loading to reach 85.7 % and achieves a cumulative release rate of 80.4 % in weakly acidic environments, demonstrating excellent potential for tumor targeted therapy [ 28 , 29 ]. In terms of functional characteristics, POSSHB hydrogel has three advantages: first, intelligent responsiveness, such as pH, temperature or enzyme triggered release; Secondly, the mechanical properties have been significantly enhanced; The third is good biocompatibility, with a cell survival rate generally exceeding 90 %. In particular, POSS-SH based hydrogel microspheres are prepared by microfluidic technology, which can effectively improve the bioavailability of insoluble drugs and promote the differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells into chondrocytes. However, these materials still face the challenge of uncontrollable degradation behavior, especially hydrolysis in alkaline environments. POSSHB-3D printing scaffold : In the field of 3D printing, POSSHB can be directly incorporated into printing materials as a modifier to construct special structures. Research has shown that 3-thiopropyl polysilsesquioxane (SSQ-SH) can increase the elongation at break of PLA by 56 % and impact strength by 37 % within the concentration range of 1-1.5 wt%, while maintaining good printability [ 30 ]. More innovative is the design of the "stiffness memory" scaffold. Through 3D printing guided thermally induced phase separation (3DTIPS) technology, POSS polyurethane scaffolds exhibit unique dynamic mechanical properties: providing sufficient mechanical support during implantation and gradually softening to match tissue modulus. This characteristic can significantly reduce stress shielding effects and promote organizational integration. However, the dispersion uniformity of POSS remains a key challenge, as concentrations exceeding 2.5 wt% can easily lead to agglomeration [ 31 ]. POSSHB bone cement : Traditional bone cement (such as PMMA) has problems such as high heat generation and toxic residue, while POSSHB bone cement completely avoids these defects through click on chemistry (click ON) and catalyst free SPAAC reaction cross-linking [ 32 , 33 ]. This type of material has three major breakthrough advantages: firstly, its biological safety is significantly improved, and it only produces mild inflammatory reactions after implantation; Secondly, porous structures (porosity>60 %) can be constructed through salt leaching and other methods to promote cell infiltration and vascular growth; Most importantly, it can load growth factors (such as BMP-2/VEGF) and nano hydroxyapatite, demonstrating osteogenic effects comparable to autogenous bone in a rabbit spinal fusion model [ 34 ]. But the main obstacle faced by clinical translation is insufficient mechanical strength. POSSHB electrospun fibers : In the field of electrospinning, the introduction of POSS nanoparticles can significantly enhance the hydrophobicity and thermal stability of electrospun fibers, improve their oil absorption performance and recyclability. For example, POSS coated polylactic acid electrospun nanofiber membranes exhibit excellent performance in oil-water separation [ 35 ]. In addition, POSS-PCUU electrospun fiber modified with ESPA protein can significantly promote endothelial cell adhesion and the expression of related markers (VE cadherin, VEGFR-2), making them suitable for small caliber vascular transplantation [ 36 ]. Long term stability remains the main obstacle to clinical application, and in the future, cross-linking strategies need to be developed to enhance the durability of fibers in bodily fluid environments. POSSHB film : POSS conjugated polymer hybrid films not only exhibit thermally stable white light emission properties, but also have good biocompatibility, making them suitable for fields such as optoelectronic devices and biosensors [ 37 ]. The optimization of mechanical properties of thin film materials is still a research focus, especially the balance between flexibility and strength. For example, POSS-SQ NPs exhibit a high photothermal conversion efficiency of 67.2 %, far exceeding most organic photothermal agents [ 40 ]. 2.1 The preparation method and structure of POSSHB used in regenerative medicine In the field of regenerative medicine, the latest preparation methods for POSSHB mainly include the following:  covalent grafting modification:  POSS is covalently attached to polymers or biomolecules through chemical reactions, such as using the epoxy groups on the surface of POSS to react with amino groups (-NH 2 ) or hydroxyl groups (-OH), and graft onto degradable polymers such as polylactic acid (PLA) or polycaprolactone (PCL) to enhance mechanical properties [ 20 ].  Click Chemistry:  CuAAC (copper catalyzed azide alkyne cycloaddition) or thiol-ene reaction is used to achieve efficient and highly selective POSS functionalization for the preparation of biosensors or drug carriers [ 21 , 22 ].  Block copolymer synthesis:  POSS is used as a monomer to participate in polymerization, such as POSS polyurethane (PU): POSS reacts with isocyanates to form hard segment reinforced elastomers for artificial blood vessels or heart valves [ 23 , 24 ]. Alternatively, POSS-PEG amphiphilic block copolymers can be constructed to prepare hydrogels for tissue repair [ 25 , 26 ].  Physical blending method:  POSS is directly dispersed into polymer matrices (such as PLA, PCL, polyvinyl alcohol), and material properties are improved by solution casting or melt blending, such as enhancing mechanical strength or regulating degradation rate [ 27 ]. To adapt to different biological application scenarios, POSSHB can be prepared into different structures, such as hydrogels, 3D printing scaffolds, bone cements, electrospun fibers, films, nanoparticles,  etc . ( Fig. 1 ).  POSSHB hydrogel:  POSSHB hydrogel is prepared by covalent bonding or physical blending, which shows superior performance characteristics to traditional hydrogel. In terms of structural design, the introduction of POSS can form a denser three-dimensional network structure. For example, the pore diameter of pH responsive SA/PEGDA/AS-POSS hydrogel prepared by Michael addition reaction decreases with the increase of POSS content, and the compression modulus increases significantly. This structural characteristic enables its drug loading to reach 85.7 % and achieves a cumulative release rate of 80.4 % in weakly acidic environments, demonstrating excellent potential for tumor targeted therapy [ 28 , 29 ]. In terms of functional characteristics, POSSHB hydrogel has three advantages: first, intelligent responsiveness, such as pH, temperature or enzyme triggered release; Secondly, the mechanical properties have been significantly enhanced; The third is good biocompatibility, with a cell survival rate generally exceeding 90 %. In particular, POSS-SH based hydrogel microspheres are prepared by microfluidic technology, which can effectively improve the bioavailability of insoluble drugs and promote the differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells into chondrocytes. However, these materials still face the challenge of uncontrollable degradation behavior, especially hydrolysis in alkaline environments. POSSHB-3D printing scaffold : In the field of 3D printing, POSSHB can be directly incorporated into printing materials as a modifier to construct special structures. Research has shown that 3-thiopropyl polysilsesquioxane (SSQ-SH) can increase the elongation at break of PLA by 56 % and impact strength by 37 % within the concentration range of 1-1.5 wt%, while maintaining good printability [ 30 ]. More innovative is the design of the "stiffness memory" scaffold. Through 3D printing guided thermally induced phase separation (3DTIPS) technology, POSS polyurethane scaffolds exhibit unique dynamic mechanical properties: providing sufficient mechanical support during implantation and gradually softening to match tissue modulus. This characteristic can significantly reduce stress shielding effects and promote organizational integration. However, the dispersion uniformity of POSS remains a key challenge, as concentrations exceeding 2.5 wt% can easily lead to agglomeration [ 31 ]. POSSHB bone cement : Traditional bone cement (such as PMMA) has problems such as high heat generation and toxic residue, while POSSHB bone cement completely avoids these defects through click on chemistry (click ON) and catalyst free SPAAC reaction cross-linking [ 32 , 33 ]. This type of material has three major breakthrough advantages: firstly, its biological safety is significantly improved, and it only produces mild inflammatory reactions after implantation; Secondly, porous structures (porosity>60 %) can be constructed through salt leaching and other methods to promote cell infiltration and vascular growth; Most importantly, it can load growth factors (such as BMP-2/VEGF) and nano hydroxyapatite, demonstrating osteogenic effects comparable to autogenous bone in a rabbit spinal fusion model [ 34 ]. But the main obstacle faced by clinical translation is insufficient mechanical strength. POSSHB electrospun fibers : In the field of electrospinning, the introduction of POSS nanoparticles can significantly enhance the hydrophobicity and thermal stability of electrospun fibers, improve their oil absorption performance and recyclability. For example, POSS coated polylactic acid electrospun nanofiber membranes exhibit excellent performance in oil-water separation [ 35 ]. In addition, POSS-PCUU electrospun fiber modified with ESPA protein can significantly promote endothelial cell adhesion and the expression of related markers (VE cadherin, VEGFR-2), making them suitable for small caliber vascular transplantation [ 36 ]. Long term stability remains the main obstacle to clinical application, and in the future, cross-linking strategies need to be developed to enhance the durability of fibers in bodily fluid environments. POSSHB film : POSS conjugated polymer hybrid films not only exhibit thermally stable white light emission properties, but also have good biocompatibility, making them suitable for fields such as optoelectronic devices and biosensors [ 37 ]. In addition, POSS modified Ti 3 C 2 T x  MXene films and chitosan-silver-octa ammonium-POSS composite films also exhibit excellent antibacterial properties and biocompatibility, making them suitable for surface modification of biomedical materials [ 38 , 39 ]. The optimization of mechanical properties of thin film materials is still a research focus, especially the balance between flexibility and strength. POSSHB nanoparticles : The application of POSS based nanoparticles in the biomedical field mainly focuses on drug delivery and photothermal therapy. For example, POSS-SQ NPs exhibit a high photothermal conversion efficiency of 67.2 %, far exceeding most organic photothermal agents [ 40 ]. More noteworthy is the PSD-FA intelligent nanoplatform, which integrates the triple functions of folate targeting, GSH responsive release, and photothermal therapy, achieving a tumor inhibition rate of 74.7 % in animal experiments [ 41 ]. The challenge of this type of material lies in the unclear metabolic behavior  in vivo , and future systematic pharmacokinetic studies are needed. Optimizing PEG modification strategies (such as degradable PEG) may improve its biological distribution. In summary, significant progress has been made in the application of POSSHB in the field of biomedical regeneration. Whether in the preparation of hydrogels, 3D printing scaffolds, bone cements, electrospun fibers, films or nanoparticles, POSSHB has shown its unique advantages and huge application potential.

2.2 Mechanical properties Mechanical properties are key parameters for designing tissue engineering scaffolds for bone tissue regeneration [ [42] ,  [43] ,  [44] ,  [45] ]. For example, as a bone substitute, the mechanical properties of the implants should match those of the tissue defect to protect the cells from destructive compression or stretching, allowing cells to develop into normal tissue. At the same time, the “stress shielding” effect should be avoided [ 46 ]. And when it is used as a nerve scaffold, the suitable flexibility can adapt to the movement of the human body, so as to avoid the physical damage caused by improper position [ 47 ]. Additionally, it should be able to bear the repeated compressive force of surrounding tissue without obvious deformation. Studies have shown that the stiffness of scaffolds can influence cell behavior [ 48 ]. The rigid nano core and multi reactive groups carried by POSS can provide a broad platform for the preparation of composite materials with adjustable and controllable mechanical properties. POSS is generally used as a filler to modify the mechanical properties of other matrix materials (synthetic polymers, natural polymers, inorganic biomaterials, and so on), especially for the synthetic polymers (polycarbonate (PC), PLA, polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), melt spun polyester based composite fiber, PNIPAM, PCL, and so on) [ [49] ,  [50] ,  [51] ,  [52] ,  [53] ]. The content of POSS has an important effect on the mechanical properties of the composites. For example, triphenyl-POSS and amino propyl isobutyl-POSS were respectively introduced into PC and PLA by melt blending method. In a low range, the tensile properties and dynamic mechanical modulus of the composites were improved with the increase of POSS content [ 54 , 55 ]. Amna et al. found that POSS nanoparticles exhibit effective nucleation effects, significantly improving the mechanical and thermal stability as well as biocompatibility of composite materials [ 56 ]. The same trend was also observed in other POSS-based hybrid materials, indicating that POSS acted as plasticizer and intensifier respectively with different content of POSS in the matrix materials [ 57 , 58 ]. In short, changing the POSS content can regulate the bending strength [ 59 ], tensile strength [ 60 , 61 ], elongation at break [ 61 , 62 ], and storage modulus [ 63 ] of the substrate material. In addition to the factors of the preparation method and the content of POSS, POSS with different end groups also affect the mechanical properties. Zhao et al. modified sodium-montmorillonite (MMT) with aminopropylisooctyl-POSS (AP-POSS) and octa ammonium-POSS (OA-POSS) respectively that could effectively control the dispersion of MTT and improve the mechanical properties of the composites by 60 % and 10 %, respectively [ 64 ]. Humeyra Sirin et al. compared the effects of POSS type and content on the mechanical properties of melt-spun polyester-based composite fibers (PET). When the content of hydroxyl-POSS was 1 wt%, the tensile modulus of the composite was increased fivefold due to the higher level of crystalline content and more oriented amorphous domains within the material. In addition, epoxy-POSS doubled the tensile modulus of PET composite fiber, while amine-POSS had no significant effect on the mechanical properties of PET [ 65 ]. The chemical structure of POSS affected its dispersion level, and then affected the mechanical properties of the composites. Octa-isobutyl-POSS was non-reactive and non-polar, and had the best dispersion among other reactive and polar POSS [ 66 ]. Additionally, Octa (3-chloroamonium propyl) silsesquioxane (OCAPS) as a physical crosslinker can enhance the toughness and compression properties of hydrogels [ 67 ]. Moreover, by incorporating bis-functionalized glycidyl propyl POSS (G-POSS) into the epoxy polymer backbone, the polymer chains are induced to self-assemble into a three-dimensional (3D) connected porous structure, significantly enhancing the mechanical properties of the material [ 68 ]. In conclusion, the mechanical strength of POSSHB can be adjusted according to the requirement of application due to the rigid character of the inorganic structure of POSS and the multi-reaction of the organic structure, which provides a strong support for the design of ideal biomedical materials.

2.3 Biodegradation behavior Biodegradation behavior of biomaterials is subjected to a series of reactions, such as hydrolysis, enzymatic hydrolysis and oxidation with the biological environment of body fluids, organic macromolecules, enzymes, free radicals, cells and so on, and gradually degraded to low molecular compounds or monomers. And then the degradation products are discharged out of the body or participate in the body's normal metabolism [ 69 ]. In comparison with natural polymers, chemical synthetic degradable materials can be used in practical applications by selecting suitable monomers or controlling the reaction conditions in the synthesis process to achieve the goal of synthesis materials [ 70 ]. POSS has significant advantages in designing ideal biodegradable biomaterials due to its unique nano-size effect and multi-reactive sites. Previous studies showed that PCL degradation was inhibited  in vitro  by POSS/PEO hybrid materials. POSS has been incorporated into many biodegradable materials and thermosetting biodegradable elastomers [ [71] ,  [72] ,  [73] ,  [74] ]. The biodegradable POSS-PCL star polymers were prepared by ring-opening polymerization of ε-caprolactone and octahydroxysiloxane, respectively by Sunny et al. The ratio of POSS and polymer can be customized to obtain polymers with ideal properties to meet tissue applications under different case conditions [ 75 ]. Erin et al. designed a linear polyurethane elastomer with short, biodegradable soft-segment and hard-segment POSS [ 76 ]. The soft segments can be introduced to control the degradation (such as PCL), while POSS will act as a physical cross-linker to link the adjacent chains together. In this way, elastomer properties can be designed by controlling the proportion of soft segments and POSS. Bagheri developed a POSS-polycaprolactone-zeolite (POSS-PCL-zeolite) nanocomposite using electrospinning technology. This POSS-PCL-zeolite nano scaffold has good biodegradability, can support the attachment and proliferation of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs), and induce bone differentiation [ 77 ]. In addition, Yong and his team electrospun a solution containing octaglycidyl polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxanes (Ope-POSS), 2-ethyl-4-methylimidazole (EMI), and PNIPAM. The resulting PNIPAM nanofiber network simulates the morphology of natural extracellular matrix (ECM), characterized by appropriate fiber diameter, pore size, and high overall porosity. It is worth noting that these nanofibers exhibit stability in aqueous environments, experiencing gradual mass loss rather than immediate dissolution, demonstrating significantly good water stability [ 78 ]. In a word, the degradation performance of POSSHB can be regulated and processed, which can meet the function demand of biomedicine and make it widely used in many fields of biomedicine.

Fig. 14 Adhesive properties : The key challenge facing current dental bonding technology is the long-term stability of the mixed layer. Due to the hydrophilic resin components and exposed collagen fibers being easily affected by hydrolysis and enzymatic hydrolysis in the oral environment, the bonding interface often gradually degrades, ultimately leading to the detachment of the restoration [ 171 ]. In response to this clinical challenge, researchers have proposed an innovative strategy of using functionalized nanomaterials to enhance adhesives. Among them, POSS have attracted much attention due to their unique biological activity characteristics - this nanomaterial can not only effectively improve the mechanical properties of the binder, but also enhance the chemical stability of the mixed layer by inducing interface mineral deposition, thereby significantly extending the clinical service life of the restoration. Biermann et al. analyzed the dentin shear bond strength (SBS) of acid etched rinse (ER) or self etched (SE) adhesives containing multifunctional polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxanes (MA-POSS-8) and found that the SBS of universal adhesives increased regardless of the concentration of MA-POSS-8. And 5 wt% MA-POSS-8 improved the SBS of ER adhesive without damaging the SBS of SE adhesive [ 172 ]. Fadaie also found that 10 wt% acrylic polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane (APOSS) as a reinforcing/crosslinking nanofiller improved the micro shear bonding strength with dentin [ 173 ]. Hydrolytic stability : Hydrolytic stability is also one of the key factors affecting the service life of resins. Chandra compared the water absorption of different types of POSS type resins and found that the water absorption capacity of methacrylate based POSS (MAPOSS) composite materials was lower than that of methacrylate-based isobutyl POSS (MIPOSS) composite materials [ 174 ]. In addition, Fadaie evaluated the effect of acrylic polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane nanostructures (APOSS) on the physical and mechanical properties, as well as hydrolysis stability of cyanoacrylate octyl ester (CA) adhesive. Adding APOSS to CA adhesive reduces solubility and water absorption. In samples containing APOSS nanostructures, degradation due to hydrolysis in water decreases after aging at 37 °C [ 173 ]. Buchwald first applied polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane modified hydroxyapatite containing methacrylate groups as fillers in dental composite materials in experiments, confirming that filler modification leads to improved quality stability of the composite materials during long-term incubation [ 175 ]. As shown in  Fig. 14 C–F, another work by Meifang Zhu's research group confirmed that the surface roughness and grafting rate of quartz fiber (QF) modified with methacrylate POSS were the highest. Furthermore, the reinforcement mechanism of SQFs POSS filled composite materials was explored, indicating that SQFs POSS filled composite materials have the best water stability and  in vitro  cell activity [ 176 ]. Other biological properties:  Rizk's team has conducted research on enhancing the biological functions of dental resins. They respectively investigated the effects of bismuth containing bioactive glass nanoparticles (BG Bi), methacryloyl functionalized polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxanes (MAPOSS), MA-POSS-8, SiO 2 @Ag, and calcium phosphate on the binder. It has been confirmed that when the particle size of POSS is less than 3 nm, POSS particles have good dispersibility, while bioactive glass particles have a strong tendency to aggregate. The addition of POSS particles does not increase or only slightly increases the viscosity of the adhesive, while bioactive glass particles significantly increase the viscosity of the adhesive. When BG Bi and multifunctional POSS were filled, the water absorption and sol portion showed a maintained or improved network structure and performance. However, less polymerization was found when loading monofunctional POSS. Multifunctional POSS can be incorporated into dental adhesives to provide bioactive potential without adversely altering material properties [ 177 ]. MA-POSS-8 has no adverse effects on material properties [ 178 ]. The addition of CAP/MA-POSS slightly increases the shear viscosity of the adhesive; The antibacterial performance remains stable and comparable to the unmodified system; In addition, improved mineral induction ability can be detected in all nanoparticle combinations [ 179 ]. In addition, Burujeny et al. chemically anchored the bactericidal 1,2,3-triazolonium functional group onto the surface of hydrophobic POSS nanoparticles (triazole POSS) and incorporated it into a dental restoration system composed of ternary thiol allyl ether methacrylate resin and glass fillers, significantly enhancing its bactericidal activity against Streptococcus mutans [ 180 ]. As shown in  Fig. 14 G–H, Gong et al. developed a light cured 3D printing scaffold material based on biomimetic design. This study successfully constructed a composite scaffold with a porous structure by combining the biomineralization characteristics of natural pearl layers, the mechanical properties of polyurethane, and the biological activity of POSS nanoparticles.  In vitro  experiments have confirmed that this new material not only effectively induces hydroxyapatite deposition, but also provides a favorable proliferation microenvironment for MC3T3-E1 pre osteoblasts. Animal experiments further showed that the stent can significantly inhibit alveolar bone resorption (with a reduction rate of 30–40 % in height and width) and promote new bone formation after implantation in the tooth extraction socket. These characteristics make it a highly promising biomaterial for alveolar ridge preservation and bone regeneration engineering [ 181 ]. In summary, POSS has shown significant advantages in the application of dental restorative materials, by reducing polymerization shrinkage, enhancing bonding performance and hydrolysis stability, while endowing the material with biological activity and antibacterial function. Although significant progress has been made in current research, the optimal dosage, long-term clinical efficacy, and synergistic mechanism with other materials of POSS still need further exploration. Multi-walled carbon nanotubes/polymer composite is a kind of mixed material, which combines many mechanical, electrical and chemical properties, so it is an ideal biomaterial for regenerative medicine [ 156 ]. Although complete dispersion of CNTs in polymer matrix was rarely achieved, Eleni V. Antoniadou et al. successfully dispersed CNTs in POSS-PCU and POSS-PCL. Within a certain range, the polymerization shrinkage rate of the modified resin was significantly reduced [ [161] ,  [162] ,  [163] ,  [164] ,  [165] ]. In addition to adding POSS alone, the combination of other nanoparticles to improve dental resins has become a new strategy. As shown in  Fig. 14 A and B, Hongyan Chen constructed MA-POSS/silica (p-SiO 2 ) hybrid particles through thiol-ene click reaction, and then used the hybrid particles as reinforcements to prepare bisphenol A glyceryl ester dimethacrylate/triacrylate copolymers. The results of mechanical properties showed that the bending modulus, compressive strength, and fracture energy of the composite material were increased by 251.2 %, 17.89 %, 122.3 %, and 1094 %, respectively, compared to the SiO 2  filled composite material. In addition, this optimal p-SiO 2  filled composite material also has better polymerization shrinkage rate, indicating that grafting MA-POSS on the surface of the filler is a promising method for surface modification of the filler, which can improve the interaction between the resin matrix/filler interface and thus enhance the comprehensive performance of the composite material [ 166 ]. A new type of dental resin composite material was developed by combining POSS with zirconia (ZrO 2 ) modified with 10-methacryloyloxydecylphosphate dihydrogen ester (10-MDP). When POSS was added at a concentration of < 4 wt%, the performance of the resin composite material was significantly improved and reached its optimal level at a concentration of 4 wt%. The development of this new resin composite material provides a new material choice for clinical applications [ 167 ]. The WeiLi Xie research group added methyl methacrylate based oligomeric silsesquioxane (MA-POSS) to a resin filled with 20 % bioactive glass. When the amount of MA-POSS added was less than 4 %, the various indicators of the composite resin material showed a dose-dependent increase. After exceeding this value, the performance began to decline. The addition of MA-POSS had no effect on the biological activity of the composite material, which means that the hybrid composite resin can perform acid neutralization, ion release, and apatite precipitation, and can be used as a smart material for clinical treatment [ 168 ]. Another work of Weili Xie's group focused on the hardness of dental resins. They prepared nano composite dental resins with different concentrations of methacryloyl polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxanes (MA-POSS) as fillers using photopolymerization method, and confirmed that the addition of a small amount of POSS significantly improved the hardness and scratch resistance of the resin matrix [ 169 ]. However, Luciano confirmed that adding 25 wt% POSS to methacrylate organic matrix does not improve the edge integrity of Class I dentin, which may affect the service life of the resin [ 170 ]. Fig. 14 Adhesive properties : The key challenge facing current dental bonding technology is the long-term stability of the mixed layer. Due to the hydrophilic resin components and exposed collagen fibers being easily affected by hydrolysis and enzymatic hydrolysis in the oral environment, the bonding interface often gradually degrades, ultimately leading to the detachment of the restoration [ 171 ]. In response to this clinical challenge, researchers have proposed an innovative strategy of using functionalized nanomaterials to enhance adhesives. Among them, POSS have attracted much attention due to their unique biological activity characteristics - this nanomaterial can not only effectively improve the mechanical properties of the binder, but also enhance the chemical stability of the mixed layer by inducing interface mineral deposition, thereby significantly extending the clinical service life of the restoration. Biermann et al. analyzed the dentin shear bond strength (SBS) of acid etched rinse (ER) or self etched (SE) adhesives containing multifunctional polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxanes (MA-POSS-8) and found that the SBS of universal adhesives increased regardless of the concentration of MA-POSS-8. And 5 wt% MA-POSS-8 improved the SBS of ER adhesive without damaging the SBS of SE adhesive [ 172 ]. Fadaie also found that 10 wt% acrylic polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane (APOSS) as a reinforcing/crosslinking nanofiller improved the micro shear bonding strength with dentin [ 173 ]. Hydrolytic stability : Hydrolytic stability is also one of the key factors affecting the service life of resins. Chandra compared the water absorption of different types of POSS type resins and found that the water absorption capacity of methacrylate based POSS (MAPOSS) composite materials was lower than that of methacrylate-based isobutyl POSS (MIPOSS) composite materials [ 174 ]. In addition, Fadaie evaluated the effect of acrylic polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane nanostructures (APOSS) on the physical and mechanical properties, as well as hydrolysis stability of cyanoacrylate octyl ester (CA) adhesive. Adding APOSS to CA adhesive reduces solubility and water absorption. In samples containing APOSS nanostructures, degradation due to hydrolysis in water decreases after aging at 37 °C [ 173 ]. Buchwald first applied polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane modified hydroxyapatite containing methacrylate groups as fillers in dental composite materials in experiments, confirming that filler modification leads to improved quality stability of the composite materials during long-term incubation [ 175 ]. As shown in  Fig. 14 C–F, another work by Meifang Zhu's research group confirmed that the surface roughness and grafting rate of quartz fiber (QF) modified with methacrylate POSS were the highest. Furthermore, the reinforcement mechanism of SQFs POSS filled composite materials was explored, indicating that SQFs POSS filled composite materials have the best water stability and  in vitro  cell activity [ 176 ]. Other biological properties:  Rizk's team has conducted research on enhancing the biological functions of dental resins. They respectively investigated the effects of bismuth containing bioactive glass nanoparticles (BG Bi), methacryloyl functionalized polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxanes (MAPOSS), MA-POSS-8, SiO 2 @Ag, and calcium phosphate on the binder. It has been confirmed that when the particle size of POSS is less than 3 nm, POSS particles have good dispersibility, while bioactive glass particles have a strong tendency to aggregate. The addition of POSS particles does not increase or only slightly increases the viscosity of the adhesive, while bioactive glass particles significantly increase the viscosity of the adhesive. When BG Bi and multifunctional POSS were filled, the water absorption and sol portion showed a maintained or improved network structure and performance. However, less polymerization was found when loading monofunctional POSS. Multifunctional POSS can be incorporated into dental adhesives to provide bioactive potential without adversely altering material properties [ 177 ]. MA-POSS-8 has no adverse effects on material properties [ 178 ]. The addition of CAP/MA-POSS slightly increases the shear viscosity of the adhesive; The antibacterial performance remains stable and comparable to the unmodified system; In addition, improved mineral induction ability can be detected in all nanoparticle combinations [ 179 ]. In addition, Burujeny et al. chemically anchored the bactericidal 1,2,3-triazolonium functional group onto the surface of hydrophobic POSS nanoparticles (triazole POSS) and incorporated it into a dental restoration system composed of ternary thiol allyl ether methacrylate resin and glass fillers, significantly enhancing its bactericidal activity against Streptococcus mutans [ 180 ]. As shown in  Fig. 14 G–H, Gong et al. developed a light cured 3D printing scaffold material based on biomimetic design. This study successfully constructed a composite scaffold with a porous structure by combining the biomineralization characteristics of natural pearl layers, the mechanical properties of polyurethane, and the biological activity of POSS nanoparticles.  In vitro  experiments have confirmed that this new material not only effectively induces hydroxyapatite deposition, but also provides a favorable proliferation microenvironment for MC3T3-E1 pre osteoblasts. Animal experiments further showed that the stent can significantly inhibit alveolar bone resorption (with a reduction rate of 30–40 % in height and width) and promote new bone formation after implantation in the tooth extraction socket. These characteristics make it a highly promising biomaterial for alveolar ridge preservation and bone regeneration engineering [ 181 ]. In summary, POSS has shown significant advantages in the application of dental restorative materials, by reducing polymerization shrinkage, enhancing bonding performance and hydrolysis stability, while endowing the material with biological activity and antibacterial function. Although significant progress has been made in current research, the optimal dosage, long-term clinical efficacy, and synergistic mechanism with other materials of POSS still need further exploration. Future research should focus on optimizing POSS functionalization strategies and developing more intelligent and durable dental restorative materials to promote their clinical translational applications.

3.7 Skeletal muscle regeneration The progress in the field of skeletal muscle tissue engineering relies on the generation of stable, life like skeletal muscle microstructures  in vitro . This requires interdisciplinary approaches to integrate cells into biological or synthetic mechanical microenvironments, enabling precise simulation of skeletal muscle function and disease, and making progress in generating transplantable tissue for treating muscle injuries and degeneration. POSS has certain application prospects in skeletal muscle repair by improving material properties, regulating cell behavior and microenvironment.  Table 7  shows the POSSHB for skeletal muscle regeneration. Amna's research shows that POSS grafted PU nanocomposites have excellent biocompatibility and can significantly promote the adhesion, proliferation, and differentiation of C2C12 myoblasts, while exhibiting antibacterial and anti-inflammatory potential. The high free energy of POSS enhances cell affinity, while the nontoxicity of nanofibers makes it an ideal biomimetic scaffold with important application prospects in the field of muscle tissue regeneration [ 56 ]. As shown in  Fig. 15 , Cheesbrough et al. developed a novel biobased nanohybrid elastomer, which forms oriented nanofiber scaffolds through electrospinning to simulate the structure and mechanical properties of the extracellular matrix of skeletal muscle cells. This material has superelasticity (ultimate strain 1000 %), elastic modulus matching natural muscles (25 kPa), and flexibility (11–50 kPa), providing an ideal mechanical microenvironment for muscle cells. Uniaxial arrangement of nanofibers effectively guides the directional growth of myoblasts, enhances sarcomere assembly, increases myotube fusion rate by 32 %, and increases muscle fiber maturity by 50 %. In addition, the scaffold can stably support the differentiation of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSC) into muscle fibers regulated by optogenetics, and exhibits significantly enhanced contractile performance under blue light stimulation: the contraction speed increases by>200 %, the specific force output increases by>280 %, and the power density reaches 35 W m −3 , far exceeding traditional culture systems. This biomimetic muscle fiber scaffold composite system provides an efficient platform for skeletal muscle tissue engineering and has important potential applications in disease modeling, drug screening, and regenerative medicine [ 182 ]. 3.8 Ophthalmic treatment In recent years, POSS have been used in the biomedical field of ophthalmology, such as contact lenses, keratitis treatment, and dry eye syndrome. In vivo  intraocular implantation experiments further confirmed that POSS material did not cause acute eye irritation or inflammatory reactions, demonstrating excellent ocular tissue compatibility. Experiments have shown that although high doses may cause oxidative stress, POSS nanomaterials have good overall safety and significant potential in ophthalmic applications such as drug carriers, artificial corneas, or retinal repair scaffolds [ 183 ]. In vitro  and  in vivo  experiments have confirmed that the material has excellent biocompatibility and safety, and its special POSS-PEG hybrid structure effectively reduces protein adhesion. This modified RCL material exhibits good clinical application potential and can be used as a candidate material for the new generation of functional corneal contact lenses [ 183 ]. 4 Conclusion and future perspectives The unique properties of POSS and its ability to combine with various polymers make it an attractive biomaterial, which has been widely explored in tissue engineering. Because of their biosecurity, biocompatibility, tunable degradability, antithrombogenicity, and the ability for loading with bioactive macromolecules, and combing with other nanoparticles, such as quantum dot nanocrystals and silver nanoparticles. In addition to the application of POSSHB in tissue regeneration discussed in this review, there are also numerous literature reports on the application of POSSHB in other biomedical fields, such as in biological imaging [ 187 , 188 ], delivery systems [ [189] ,  [190] ,  [191] ,  [192] ,  [193] ], tumor therapy [ 40 , [194] ,  [195] ,  [196] ,  [197] ], biosensors [ 198 , 199 ], biological adhesives [ 179 , 200 ]. In future research, POSSHB still has great potential for expansion in structural design and biological applications. In terms of structural innovation, multi-level ordered micro nano structures can be constructed through biomimetic strategies, such as developing POSSHB scaffolds with gradient porosity or anisotropic mechanical properties, to better simulate the structural characteristics of complex tissues such as tendons and corneas. In addition, introducing dynamic covalent chemistry (such as imine bonds and disulfide bonds) into the POSSHB network can endow the material with intelligent properties such as self-healing and shape memory, making it suitable for dynamic biological environments. In emerging application fields, POSSHB has significant potential in organoid construction, and its precise mechanical and biochemical signal regulation ability can provide a biomimetic microenvironment for stem cells; In the field of immune regulation, it is expected to be used for the treatment of autoimmune diseases by modifying anti-inflammatory factors (such as IL-4) or regulating the surface topology of materials; In the direction of neural interfaces, conductive POSSHB (such as poly pyrrole) can promote neural signal transduction and be used for spinal cord injury repair. In addition, the development of POSSHB bioinks will drive the process of 3D bioprinting complex organs. However, it is a long way to apply POSSHB to clinic. First, the toxicity of these biomaterials should be studied in detail. Secondly, how to achieve the balance between the various functions to achieve the ideal application effect is still a certain degree of challenge. Finally, close collaboration between scientists and clinicians is critical to understanding the underlying mechanisms of cell-biomaterial interactions at the nanoscale level and to be able to translate research findings from the workbench to the bedside. The future of POSSHB may lie in the further study of its mechanism of action, toxic effect and the balance between its functions, which will lay a foundation for its clinical application. Overall, POSSHB, with its unique structural designability and multifunctional integration capabilities, is bringing revolutionary innovation opportunities to the biomedical field. However, its clinical translation still requires breakthrough progress in basic research and application development.
